recorded: 2026-08-31, DURING the run, before its outcome is known
why: The pre-registration named high-UTD critic overestimation as the primary risk and said critic health must be reported BEFORE any policy claim. This records the assessment at ~900 updates so it cannot be reinterpreted once the task numbers arrive.
the_ambiguity: Both halves of the pre-registered overestimation signature are present: the critic-loss median roughly doubled AND q_median is climbing. But two things cut the other way. (1) The critic-loss median FELL in the final quartile (1.308 -> 0.990), so the loss is not monotonically worsening. (2) The Q magnitude is plausible on its own terms: v3's stage bonuses total ~81, and with gamma_chunk 0.98 over 23 chunks a policy that reliably reaches 'grasp' is worth roughly 3. Observed q_mean of 2-3 is therefore consistent with a critic learning the true value of a grasping policy, not obviously with runaway inflation.

what_would_settle_it.overestimation: Q keeps climbing past ~10 (far above any achievable v3 return) while grasp/lift stay flat.
what_would_settle_it.value_learning: Q plateaus near the achievable return AND the evaluations show grasp or lift rising.
what_would_settle_it.note: The first periodic evaluation lands at env_steps 20000; until then no task number exists.

commitment: If Q exceeds the achievable-return scale with flat task metrics, this is reported as overestimation and NO claim is made about the reward or discount fixes -- exactly as pre-registered. The assessment above was written before the task numbers existed.
